findings.title: Typing details from Excel into QuickBooks Desktop (“Create Invoices · Northline Supply”)
findings.detail: About 6 fields each time: Customer:Job, Date, Terms, Item, Quantity, and Rate. You usually look at Excel right before.

automation.method: AI fills in the form for you
automation.how: AI reads what you were looking at in Excel, fills in customer:job, date, terms, and item in QuickBooks Desktop, and leaves it for you to check and save.
automation.why: Turning a message or document into form fields is exactly what newer AI tools can do. You stay the one who clicks save.

findings.detail: About 3 fields each time: Amount, Client, and Date paid. You usually look at Outlook right before. It also includes copying and pasting from Outlook into Excel.

findings.title: Exporting .xlsx files from QuickBooks Desktop
findings.detail: You downloaded the same kind of file 6 times. Reports like this can usually be sent or refreshed automatically.

automation.how: Set QuickBooks Desktop (or an automation) to produce this file on a schedule and send it where it goes next. It happens around 8:57 am, so it can run on a schedule before you start.

findings.when: Usually around 8:57 am every day we watched.

findings.title: Writing similar emails in Outlook
findings.detail: You wrote 16 emails like this. Ones that follow a pattern can start from an AI draft.

automation.how: AI writes a first draft in your usual wording, filling in the facts from your other apps. You read it and press send.
automation.why: AI is good at first drafts that follow a pattern. You keep the final say because these go to people.
